title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative: Between March 2020, Solomon Islands Chamber of Commerce and Industry undertook an assessment on the impact of COVID19 on members reaching 102 firms of different size and sector through survey - the first enterprise-based COVID impact study of its kind in the Solomon Islands. The study found over 400 workers faced redundancy due to enterprise closures and COVID driven down-sizing. Based on the findings, SCCI produced a newsletter in April 2020 sharing the findings with members, and in May 2020 published a press release. Through the SI Government Private Sector Advisory Group, the COVID Oversight Committee, and the Royal Solomon Islands Police Force-SICCI Executive Group, the Chamber also engaged in direct advocacy for key recommendations to be included in the stimulus package and related support measures. These recommendations included reduction of the electricity tariff, more timely payment by Government to its suppliers, reduction of port charges and those related to cargo for provincial areas; tax relief for businesses impacted by COVID; deferred loan repayments and extended loan terms; and additional policy measures to support SMEs. As a result of this strengthened capability for research and analysis, SICCI has conducted ongoing monitoring of the impacts of COVID in December 2020 reaching 526 enterprises, July 2021 reaching 63 enterprises, and September 2021 reaching 200 enterprises covering approximately 80% of the private sector workforce. Following evidence-based recommendations put forward by SICCI's based on these studies, a number of reforms have been implemented by Government including a reduction of the electricity tariff and economic relief for businesses as part of the stimulus package. Since April 2020, 15 additional research projects have been undertaken by SICCI with 1,030 responses from enterprises on topics ranging from proposed and enacted policy measures, business confidence, through to feedback on Chamber events and activities. In April 2020, the ILO assisted SICCI for the design of surveys to assess the impact of COVID; delivered training and coaching sessions on use of the Qualtrics software for survey distribution, analysis and reporting; and supported the final analysis and report drafting. In July and August 2021, the ILO provided additional training and coaching sessions on the Qualtrics software to upskill the capacity of the CEO, the Advocacy Officer, the Membership and Services Officer, and the Export Industry Development Officer for advanced data analytics and dashboarding of findings. Further assistance to SICCI this biennium included collaboration with the ITC-ILO to provide the Chamber with customized Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software and training on its use for the secretariats membership and services unit; production of a quick reference guide to common COVID response policy measures and its adaption and tailoring by the Pacific Island Private Sector Organization (PIPOS) in November 2020; trainings between December 2020 and September 2021 in partnership with the ITC-ILO on lobbying and advocacy, membership strategies, and the role of wages and productivity in pathways to sustainable recovery; and the launch of a Pacific eCampus for Pacific employers and business membership organizations in May 2021.
